About Us

In 2006, Rancher Pati Jacobs took over the cattle business on the family ranch with a singular focus on raising grass-fed beef. Not content with the traditional distribution channels (i.e. auctions & feedlots) Pati decided to make her own company to directly sell her beef to her Central Texas neighbors. 

Many years later, Bastrop Cattle Company has grown to accommodate more of the increasing demand for grass-fed beef without sacrificing any of the quality, principle, or personal touch that made it successful in the first place.

When you buy from Bastrop Cattle Company, you’re buying nutritious, rich grass-fed beef directly from the 3 ranchers who run the company.

There’s a simple joy in buying food directly from the people who made it.
View fullsize

One would be hard pressed to find someone who wouldn’t want to buy their groceries from local ranchers and farmers. There’s so much comfort in the simplicity of buying direct, and yet it’s very difficult for most people to do so. Even trying to find out where your food comes from can be an exhausting exercise.

In 2003, When Pati Jacobs took over her family ranch in Bastrop, Texas, she wanted keep things simple. During her childhood she had seen the joy that raising cattle had brought her parents, but also the stress they endured due to fluctuating cattle prices at the auction barn. Prices could drop 80% in a week, and it made managing the finances difficult. She didn’t want to base her business on an unstable market.

On an ethical level, Pati didn’t like the use of grain/corn especially in feedlot production. Cows are ruminant animals, and their bodies aren’t designed to process anything other than foliage. As stewards of land and livestock, Pati believes that ranchers should strive to provide a natural, comfortable existence for their herds. 

View fullsize

Lastly, Pati felt morally responsible to preserve the natural biodiversity of the land and limit the environmental impact of her business. So much has been written about the damaging impacts of fertilizer and pesticides on soil. Additionally much discussion about climate change has focused on emissions from cattle production. But how could a ranching operation address these issues?

For all her research, the answer was simple. Feed cows grass, process at a local butcher, deliver to local customers. What might surprise you is that it’s not only the right thing to do ethically, it’s also financially the best way for small ranchers to stay in business. 

Many agricultural products like hormones, fertilizer, etc, might provide a short term boost to cattle weight but don’t work in the long run. Healthy soil makes healthy grass that naturally pushes out weeds. Cattle that have abundant access to grass, water and shade experience stress-free lives that keep them fat and happy. 

Pati has always felt that so much of agricultural industry is smoke and mirrors, profiteering off the backs of small family farms and ranches. Ironically this corporate greed is why so many small producers go out of business. 4 massive companies control over 80% of the beef production in the U.S. It’s bad for the workers, it’s bad for the ranchers and it’s bad for the cattle. 

The food system doesn’t need to be complicated. After all these years, Bastrop Cattle Company still runs a simple operation. We raise the cattle on grass, we butcher at a local family-owned facility, then deliver it to you. Period.

There’s a lot of bull in the beef industry,
we don’t do that.

Delivery Info
View fullsize

BCC includes free shipping on all combination boxes. Half/Whole cow orders are delivered for free within our delivery range, otherwise they can be picked up, Shipping for halves/whole cows is available at an additional cost.

The order is shipped via UPS. The beef is packed in a styrofoam cooler inside of a recyclable cardboard box. We pack it hard frozen and verify the recipient will be home to receive the delivery.

What to expect upon arrival

Customers should expect beef that is cold to the touch, NOT entirely frozen, especially those in 2 day range, as is standard for all meat delivery by mail. 

+ It should look and feel like beef that you just brought back from the grocery store. The standard is refrigerated coldness of 38 degrees or colder.

+ Thinner/smaller cuts are likely to have defrosted. They should be still clearly cold to the touch and look appealing.

+ The difference between a slightly defrosted cut and a entirely defrosted compromised cut is that the blood has completely left the entire cut and is pooling at the bottom of the package and the meat has lost its color. This is still likely “usable” but not ideal and not what you paid for. If this happens, please contact us and we will always make it right!

Our Guarantee To You

If you ever receive a package that is not at top quality, we will always make it right. As a company that ships a refrigerated product via mail, we can’t always control what happens in transit. However, we know you’re spending your hard earned money to support our small business. So in the event of an issue, you can be assured that we will either replace any/all affected cuts or refund your order if you’d like. As company policy, we never force customers to pay for beef that they cannot use. We don’t just want the one-time sale, we want to be your trusted provider for years to come.

Can I pick up my combination box order?

You can always request a pickup in the special notes field at checkout. We keep all of our inventory in our freezer in Schulenburg, so please note that if you are wanting to pick up at the ranch, it will extend the wait time a little because we have to bring it back and coordinate a pickup (as opposed to us packaging it and dropping it off with UPS direct from our freezer). Customers who live in Bastrop or right nearby are automatically going to be considered either a pickup or local delivery. Pickups do not decrease turnaround, they slightly extend it.

Combination Box /Beef Quarter Shipping

Free UPS for all Combination Boxes and Beef Quarters in Texas

Arrives at your door (no signature required). We text to confirm the day before that you will be at the address before we ship.

If there is an unexpected delay or your order is damaged in transit, we are always willing to either replace or refund. 

Our inventory is stored in Schulenburg and we do not have a farm stand, so we do not generally offer pickup, but you can always request it in the special notes field at checkout. Bastrop area customers can pickup, or we can personally bring it to your door!

Half/Whole Cow Delivery/Shipping

Free in-person delivery to areas within our delivery zone.
Currently this includes Austin & surrounding areas, San Antonio & surrounding areas, and of course Bastrop & Surrounding areas. Contact us if you’re unsure about your address!

Free pick up at our Ranch in Bastrop or our office in Schulenburg

Shipping via UPS is available for half/whole customers in Texas for an additional $1.20/lb. Areas outside of Texas will require a custom quote.
